📌 Description

This PR fixes a broken access control vulnerability in api/graphql_schema.py:208-302 and api/main.py:195-197 where GraphQL resolvers exposed application data and mutations without authentication or authorization enforcement.

Previously, the GraphQL implementation trusted attacker-controlled identifiers directly and exposed the schema publicly:

Resolvers accepted attacker-controlled user_id and case_id parameters
No authentication dependency was enforced
No ownership validation was performed
Arbitrary user data could be queried directly
Mutations operated on attacker-supplied resource identifiers
graphiql=True exposed the full schema publicly

Because the GraphQL API trusted user-supplied identifiers without validating authenticated user context or ownership, unauthenticated callers could query or modify arbitrary application data.

Current behavior before the fix:

Any user’s case data could be queried without authorization
Sensitive documents and records were exposed publicly
Mutations could modify or delete arbitrary application data
Authorization scope depended entirely on attacker-controlled input
GraphQL resolvers bypassed application access control guarantees
Public schema exposure simplified endpoint enumeration and exploitation

If an attacker submitted crafted GraphQL queries or mutations with arbitrary user_id or case_id values, they could retrieve or manipulate data belonging to other users without authentication.

As a result:

Any user’s case data could be queried without authorization
Sensitive documents and records could be exposed publicly
Unauthorized mutations could modify or delete arbitrary data
GraphQL became a direct broken-access-control vector
Complete application data compromise became possible
Authorization guarantees became inconsistent across API surfaces

The updated implementation enforces authenticated access, validates ownership consistently, and restricts GraphQL exposure to authorized application contexts.

With these changes:

GraphQL endpoints now require authenticated access
Resolvers enforce ownership and authorization checks consistently
User identity derives from authenticated session context
Attacker-supplied identifiers no longer determine authorization scope
Unauthorized queries and mutations are rejected safely
Production deployments restrict unnecessary schema exposure features

✨ Changes Included

Added authentication enforcement for GraphQL endpoints
Integrated ownership validation into GraphQL resolvers
Removed reliance on attacker-controlled authorization identifiers
Restricted unauthorized query and mutation access
Hardened GraphQL access control behavior across resolvers
Disabled unnecessary schema exposure features for production environments

🧪 Testing Done

Verified unauthenticated GraphQL requests are rejected correctly
Tested ownership enforcement across query and mutation resolvers
Confirmed unauthorized resource access is blocked safely
Validated authenticated users can access only permitted resources
Tested GraphQL mutation authorization behavior
Confirmed no regressions in authorized GraphQL functionality

closes #1215
